title: First Touch Speed Framework and Boarding Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, skimmable operational framework for accelerating 'first touch' (candidate reply -> hiring decision cadence) while preserving candidate experience and early role readiness. Use as a one-pager for recruiters, hiring managers, and the interview panel.

Audience:
- People Ops recruiters and hiring partners
- Hiring managers and interviewers
- Onboarding buddy / manager for new ICs

Design goals (what we're optimizing for):
- Time to decision: reduce wasted wait states between interview stages
- Candidate experience: fast, transparent communications and clear next steps
- New hire readiness: compact preboarding to get folks productive in week 1
- Low friction for interviewers: short rubrics and clear eval windows

Quick schematic (timeline):
- Day -7 to -1 (Offer accepted -> start date): "Preboard Sprint" (see checklist)
- Day 0 (Start): Welcome rituals + environment check (30–60m)
- Week 0: Essentials (accounts, quickwins, meetings)
- Week 1: Shadow + first small delivery
- Week 2–4: Ramp plan milestones + 1:1 cadence

Preboard Sprint (immediately after offer accept):
- Recruiter: send preboard packet within 24h (contract + basic first-week agenda + buddy intro)
- Hiring manager: confirm start week schedule and identify 2 first-week tasks (<= 4h each)
- Infra/SRE: request account provisioning 5 business days before start; escalate if not complete by Day -2
- Head of Security: verify KMS/HSM access path is provisioned if private deployment role
- Buddy: send intro note + optional calendar invite for Day 0 orientation
- People Ops: create profile in HRIS, set payroll, benefits reminders, and setup new-hire tracker

Preboard sample message (recruiter to new hire):
Hi <Name>, congrats again and excited to have you join Redwood Inference. Attached is a short preboard packet with what to expect on day one and a checklist of small tasks you can complete before you start (optional). If you have any questions about equipment, travel, or paperwork, reply here and I’ll coordinate. —Priya

Day 0 ritual (30–60 minutes):
- Welcome (5–10m): Hiring manager + buddy welcome, context, high-level product orientation
- Admin check (10–15m): accounts, VPN/KMS, HRIS confirmation
- First micro-task handoff (15–30m): explain first-week task, acceptance criteria, expected reviewers
- Quick sync (5–10m): set weekly 1:1 and buddy check-ins

Week 1 essentials (sample schedule):
- Mon: orientation + micro-task kickoff
- Tue–Thu: shadowing sessions with cross-functional partners (platform, infra, product)
- Fri: demo of first micro-task + feedback session

Interview rubric (compact, 5–7 minutes per evaluator to fill):
- Role fit (1–5): did candidate show core domain fluency?
- Problem solving (1–5): structured approach + tradeoff awareness
- Communication (1–5): clarity, concision, cross-team storytelling
- Production judgment (1–5): deployment, observability, reliability considerations
- Recommendation: Strong hire / Hire with caveats / Pass
- Mandatory free-text: 1–2 line primary risk or signal

Panel operations (best practices):
- Schedule windows of 48–72 hours for interview rounds; avoid >5 business days delay
- Use our short rubric only; long matrices deter panel completion
- Interviewers must submit evaluations within 24 hours of interview or get auto-reminder
- Calibrate monthly: 30 minute sync with hiring managers + 3 sample evals to align scoring

Recruiting KPIs we track locally (people ops):
- Time to first interview (target < 4 business days from application/intro)
- Time from first interview to onsite/loop decision (target < 10 business days)
- Offer acceptance to start lag (median target 21 days)
- New hire first 30-day throughput (task completions vs expected)

Micro-onboarding checklist (Day -7 -> Day 7):
- Hardware: confirm shipping + ETA, provide loaner if ETA > start date
- Accounts: email, GitHub, Redwood Console staging access, Slack, HRIS (confirm by Day 0)
- Security training: send link to training module; completion target Day 7
- First repo & PR: assign a tiny starter issue with a reviewer (clear acceptance criteria)
- Documentation: assign 3 docs to read (product overview, infra runbook, team README)

Interviewer quick calibration script (2 mins):
1) Rate the candidate on the 4 rubric dims (1–5).
2) Answer: "Would I pair with this person on a small delivery within 2 weeks? Y/N"
3) Note one clear risk and one clear signal (one sentence each).

Manager checklist for week 0–4 ramp (copyable):
- Day 0: intro + expectations + micro-task assigned
- End Week 1: demo + feedback + set 30-day goals
- End Week 2: stakeholder intros complete + first cross-team pairing
- End Week 4: evaluate for independent feature work and update IC growth plan

Edge cases & notes to self (informal):
- If account provisioning stalled, escalate to infra on-call with ticket ID and start date; do not let new hire wait >48h.
- For private deployment hires (high compliance), add an extra compliance sign-off step in preboard for KYC/KMS.
- Consider offering a 2-hour pre-start architecture deep-dive for senior hires to shorten the ramp.
- Unresolved: should we centralize preboard packets per role or per band? (tradeoffs: maintenance vs specificity)

Templates and snippets (copy/paste):
- Short candidate follow-up after loop: "Thanks for interviewing with Redwood Inference. We expect to share a decision by <date>. If you have any follow-ups, reply here."
- Offer acceptance confirmation: include buddy contact, Day 0 schedule, equipment ETA, and an attachable preboard checklist PDF

Implementation notes for People Ops team (action items):
- Create a canonical preboard Google Doc template (Confluence link above is working draft)
- Ship a short Slack workflow to remind interviewers to submit evaluations after 24h
- Build a tiny Linear pipeline for "preboard provisioning" to track account completion in real time

Open questions for next review (people-ops retrospective):
- Are our micro-tasks sufficiently representative of the first 90 days outcomes?
- Does a 21-day median offer->start target cause repeated provisioning crunches? Data check needed.
- Should we mandate a 1-week paid early access for senior hires to do architecture onboarding?

Notes: this doc is intentionally terse and pragmatic. Treat as a living cheatsheet — copyable checklists and short rubrics are higher signal than long playbooks for busy hiring managers.

End of doc.
